\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The phenomenon}

Consider a recurrent cell trained to perform column-wise addition with carries.
Trained at unroll depth $n=5$ it is exact; evaluated deeper its accuracy decays,
\[
n=5:\ 1.0000 \qquad n=6:\ 0.9556 \qquad n=7:\ 0.1445 \qquad n=8:\ 0.0166,
\]
with column-clustered errors: the model loses positional alignment part way
through the sum. We call this the \emph{carry wall}. A standard intervention is
an explicit boundary (``end-of-sequence'') token: a learned embedding of width
$E$, zero-padded to the input width $N=384$, appended to the digit stream. The
digit vocabulary occupies the first $D=20$ coordinates. Everything else is held
fixed; only $E$ varies.

\subsection{The apparent threshold and its refutation}

A sweep over $E\in\{20,28,64,96,128,192,256,384\}$ with two initialisations each
gives, at $E=20$, accuracies $0.9990$ and $0.0166$; at every $E\ge 28$, fourteen
out of fourteen runs at $1.0000$. Read naively this says there is a width
threshold between $20$ and $28$.

Extending the $E=20$ arm to twelve runs destroys that reading. The twelve
accuracies, in basis points ($10^{-4}$ units), are
\[
9990,\ 9990,\ 9990,\ 7440,\ 1240,\ 580,\ 310,\ 260,\ 170,\ 110,\ 60,\ 50 .
\]
Three are clean cures; nine are not; all twelve have width $20$. A threshold
model asserts the outcome is a function of the width, and a function cannot take
two values at one input.

\subsection{Contributions}

\begin{enumerate}
\item A deterministic no-threshold theorem, with a reusable equal-width-split
obstruction (\S\ref{sec:nothreshold}).
\item A one-sided stochastic-dominance law with quantified evidence: a
confidence bound for the robust regime and a uniform likelihood-ratio rejection
of the homogeneous null (\S\ref{sec:stats}).
\item An exact tropical dichotomy --- span membership iff absence of an
exclusive dimension --- with an ambiguity theorem, a uniform margin bound and
its sharpness (\S\ref{sec:mechanism}).
\item An exact separability criterion, $\max_i c_i>0$, with the resulting
interior and degenerate cure probabilities and their monotonicity in $E$
(\S\ref{sec:prob}).
\item Depth-uniform non-amplification, explaining the smooth collapse
(\S\ref{sec:depth}).
\item Corrections to two earlier claims and a diagnostic probe consistent with
the mechanism (\S\ref{sec:diag}).
\end{enumerate}

\section{Setup and notation}

\subsection{The max-plus semiring}

Let $\Rbar=\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$ with
\[
a\oplus b:=\max(a,b),\qquad a\odot b:=a+b,
\]
tropical zero $-\infty$ and tropical one $0$. This is the \emph{max-plus} or
\emph{tropical} semiring: the natural algebra of piecewise-linear, max-taking
computation, in which $-\infty$ encodes ``this coordinate is not used.''

\begin{definition}[Tropical vector]
A \emph{tropical vector of width $N$} is a map $x:\{0,\dots,N-1\}\to\Rbar$; we
write $x_i$ for its $i$-th coordinate.
\end{definition}

\subsection{Tokens}

Fix an ambient width $N$ and a digit-block width $D\le N$.

\begin{definition}[Digit atom]
For $j<D$, the \emph{digit atom} $\delta^{(j)}$ has $\delta^{(j)}_j=0$ and
$\delta^{(j)}_i=-\infty$ for $i\ne j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Tropical combination and span]
For $\lambda_0,\dots,\lambda_{D-1}\in\Rbar$,
\[
\Big(\bigoplus_j \lambda_j\odot\delta^{(j)}\Big)_i
= \max_{j<D}\big(\lambda_j+\delta^{(j)}_i\big).
\]
The set of all such vectors is the \emph{digit span} $\Spanop(\delta)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Exclusive dimension]
A coordinate $p$ is an \emph{exclusive dimension} of $x$ if $p\ge D$ and
$x_p\ne-\infty$. We say $x$ \emph{has no exclusive dimension} if $x_i=-\infty$
for all $i\ge D$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Zero-padded boundary token]
$\varepsilon^{(E)}_i = 0$ for $i<E$ and $-\infty$ for $i\ge E$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Learned block-supported boundary token]
Given real coefficients $c=(c_0,\dots,c_{D-1})$, set $\eta^{(c)}_i=c_i$ for
$i<D$ and $\eta^{(c)}_i=-\infty$ for $i\ge D$. This models a boundary embedding
learned from a random initialisation whose support lies inside the digit block
($E\le D$).
\end{definition}

\subsection{Readouts and separation}

\begin{definition}[Max-plus readout]
For weights $w$, the \emph{score} of $x$ is
$\sco_w(x):=\max_{i<N}(w_i+x_i)=\bigoplus_i w_i\odot x_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Probe]
The readout listening only to coordinate $p$ with gain $g$ is $\pi^{p,g}_i=g$
if $i=p$ and $-\infty$ otherwise; directly, $\sco_{\pi^{p,g}}(x)=g+x_p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Separability]
\label{def:sep}
A boundary vector $x$ is \emph{separable} if there is a readout $w$ with
$\sco_w(\delta^{(j)})<\sco_w(x)$ for every $j<D$.
\end{definition}

Separability formalises ``the network can in principle learn a channel that
recognises the boundary as a category of its own.'' The readout is quantified
\emph{existentially}: separation is a property of the \emph{learnable} readout,
not of a random one (see \S\ref{sec:disc}).

\subsection{The experimental record}

\emph{Fragile sample} ($E=20$, twelve runs, basis points):
$9990,9990,9990,7440,1240,580,310,260,170,110,60,50$.
\emph{Robust sample} ($E\ge 28$, twenty runs): $E\in\{28,64,96,128,192,256,384\}$
at two seeds each plus $E=384$ at six further seeds; all $10000$.

\begin{definition}[Cure]
A run is \emph{cured} if its accuracy is at least $9000$ basis points. For a
sample $L$ and level $t$, $T(L,t)$ is the number of entries $\ge t$.
\end{definition}

\section{There is no sharp width boundary}\label{sec:nothreshold}

\begin{definition}[Sharp-boundary model]
A collection of runs, each with a width and a cure outcome, satisfies a
\emph{sharp-boundary model} if there is $E_0$ with: cured $\iff$ width $\ge E_0$,
for every run.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Equal-width split obstruction]\label{thm:split}
If a collection of runs contains two runs $a,b$ of the same width with $a$ cured
and $b$ not cured, then no sharp-boundary model holds.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Suppose $E_0$ witnesses the model. Since $a$ is cured,
$E_0\le\mathrm{width}(a)=\mathrm{width}(b)$; applying the equivalence to $b$ in
the other direction makes $b$ cured, a contradiction.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[No sharp boundary for the observed data]
The thirty-two-run data set admits no sharp-boundary model.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The runs of width $20$ with accuracies $9990$ and $170$ are both present; the
first is cured and the second is not. Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:split}.
\end{proof}

This refutation is deterministic: it uses no distributional assumption and no
significance level. The proposed law simply has the wrong \emph{type}.

\section{The correct law: a one-sided distribution shift}\label{sec:stats}

\subsection{Cure rates}

\begin{proposition}[Empirical cure rates]
$T(L_{20},9000)=3$ out of $12$, a rate of $1/4$; $T(L_{\ge 28},9000)=20$ out of
$20$, a rate of $1$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Exactly the entries $9990,9990,9990$ of the fragile sample meet the threshold,
and every robust entry equals $10000$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Fragile median]
The median of the fragile sample --- the mean of its two central order
statistics $310$ and $580$ --- is $445$ basis points, i.e.\ $0.0445$.
\end{proposition}

Thus the typical fragile run is not a near-miss but a total failure: the sample
is strongly bimodal.

\subsection{Stochastic dominance}

\begin{theorem}[One-sided distribution shift]\label{thm:dom}
For every accuracy level $t$,
\[
\frac{T(L_{20},t)}{12}\ \le\ \frac{T(L_{\ge28},t)}{20}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $t\le 10000$, every robust entry is $\ge t$ so the right side is $1$, while
the left side is at most $1$. If $t>10000>9990$, no fragile entry attains $t$,
so the left side is $0$ and the right side is nonnegative.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Strictness at the cure level]
$T(L_{20},9000)/12 = 3/12 < 1 = T(L_{\ge28},9000)/20$.
\end{theorem}

Together these are the precise content of ``one-sided distribution shift'':
widening never decreases any tail fraction and strictly increases the one that
matters.

\subsection{How strong is $20/20$?}

\begin{theorem}[Robust-regime confidence]
Under an i.i.d.\ Bernoulli model with per-run cure probability $p$, if
$0\le p\le 0.86$ then $p^{20}\le 0.86^{20}<0.05$. Hence the one-sided $5\%$ test
rejects every $p\le0.86$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$t\mapsto t^{20}$ is monotone on $[0,\infty)$ and $0.86^{20}\approx0.0456$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Rejecting the homogeneous null}

Under a single-probability null the likelihood of the data is
$\binom{12}{3}p^{23}(1-p)^9$ (twenty-three successes, nine failures); the
two-regime alternative attains $\binom{12}{3}(1/4)^3(3/4)^9\cdot 1^{20}$.

\begin{lemma}[Exponential weighted AM--GM]\label{lem:amgm}
For $a\ge0$, $c>0$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
$a^n\le c^n\exp\big(n(a/c)-n\big)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
From $1+u\le e^u$ with $u=a/c-1$ we get $a/c\le e^{a/c-1}$, hence
$a\le c\,e^{a/c-1}$; raise to the $n$-th power.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Maximum of the pooled binomial kernel]\label{thm:kernel}
For $p\in[0,1]$,
\[
p^{23}(1-p)^{9}\ \le\ \Big(\tfrac{23}{32}\Big)^{23}\Big(\tfrac{9}{32}\Big)^{9}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:amgm} to $a=p$ with $c=23/32$, $n=23$, and to $a=1-p$ with
$c=9/32$, $n=9$. Multiplying the nonnegative bounds and noting
$(32p-23)+(32(1-p)-9)=0$, the exponentials cancel to $1$.
\end{proof}

The maximiser $p=23/32$ is exactly the pooled success frequency $23/(23+9)$.

\begin{theorem}[Uniform rejection of the homogeneous null]
For every $p\in[0,1]$,
\[
10^{5}\cdot p^{23}(1-p)^{9}\ \le\ \Big(\tfrac14\Big)^{3}\Big(\tfrac34\Big)^{9}\cdot 1^{20}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:kernel} it suffices that
$10^{5}(23/32)^{23}(9/32)^{9}\le(1/4)^{3}(3/4)^{9}$: the left side is about
$1.4\times10^{-4}$ and the right about $1.2\times10^{-3}$. The factor
$\binom{12}{3}$ cancels on both sides.
\end{proof}

The two regimes are therefore genuinely different distributions, while neither
is a deterministic function of width.

\section{The mechanism: tropical separation theory}\label{sec:mechanism}

\subsection{The span dichotomy}

\begin{theorem}[Span dichotomy]\label{thm:span}
Let $D\le N$ and let $x$ be a tropical vector of width $N$. Then
$x\in\Spanop(\delta^{(0)},\dots,\delta^{(D-1)})$ if and only if $x$ has no
exclusive dimension.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
($\Rightarrow$) If $x=\bigoplus_j\lambda_j\odot\delta^{(j)}$ and $i\ge D$, every
term $\lambda_j+\delta^{(j)}_i$ is $-\infty$ because $j<D\le i$; the maximum of
an all-$(-\infty)$ family is $-\infty$.
($\Leftarrow$) Take $\lambda_j:=x_j$. For $i<D$ the family is $-\infty$ except
at $j=i$, where it equals $x_i+0$; for $i\ge D$ the combination is $-\infty$,
which equals $x_i$ by hypothesis.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
A boundary vector with an exclusive dimension is not a tropical combination of
digit atoms.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Zero-padded tokens]\label{cor:eosspan}
For $D<N$: $\varepsilon^{(E)}\in\Spanop(\delta)$ if and only if $E\le D$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If $E\le D$ then $\varepsilon^{(E)}_i=-\infty$ for $i\ge D$. If $E>D$ then
coordinate $D$ exists and $\varepsilon^{(E)}_D=0\ne-\infty$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Width is not the control variable]
For $0<D<N$ there exist two tropical vectors, each with tropical support of size
one, one in the digit span and one not.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take $\delta^{(0)}$, which lies in the span, and $\pi^{D,0}$, which has an
exclusive dimension at $D$.
\end{proof}

Two tokens of \emph{identical} size sit on opposite sides of the dichotomy: size
is not what matters, \emph{where} the mass sits is.

\subsection{Readouts cannot see a span member}

\begin{theorem}[Ambiguity theorem]\label{thm:ambig}
Let $x$ have no exclusive dimension. Then for every readout $w$,
\[
\sco_w(x)=\max_{j<D}\Big(x_j+\sco_w(\delta^{(j)})\Big).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
First $\sco_w(\delta^{(j)})=w_j$, since in $\max_i(w_i+\delta^{(j)}_i)$ every
term but $i=j$ is $-\infty$. So the right side is $\max_{j<D}(w_j+x_j)$. On the
left, terms with $i\ge D$ contribute $-\infty$ and may be dropped; the remaining
terms are exactly those on the right.
\end{proof}

Interpretation: the response of any readout to a boundary token inside the digit
block is a fixed tropical combination of its digit responses, with coefficients
determined by the token alone. No readout has a channel that hears the boundary
but no digit.

\begin{theorem}[Uniform margin bound]\label{thm:margin}
Let $x$ have no exclusive dimension. Then for every readout $w$,
\[
\sco_w(x)\ \le\ \Big(\max_{j<D}x_j\Big)+\max_{j<D}\sco_w(\delta^{(j)}).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Bound each term in Theorem~\ref{thm:ambig} by replacing $x_j$ with
$\max_{j'}x_{j'}$ and $\sco_w(\delta^{(j)})$ with
$\max_{j'}\sco_w(\delta^{(j')})$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Sharpness of the margin bound]\label{thm:sharp}
Let $\eta^{(c)}$ be a learned block-supported token with $D\ge1$. There exists a
readout attaining equality in Theorem~\ref{thm:margin}; consequently the best
achievable boundary-versus-digit margin is exactly $\max_j c_j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $i$ maximise $c$ and take $w=\pi^{i,0}$. Then $\sco_w(\eta^{(c)})=c_i=\max_j
c_j$, while $\sco_w(\delta^{(j)})=\delta^{(j)}_i$, which is $0$ if $j=i$ and
$-\infty$ otherwise, so the maximum over $j$ is $0$. Both sides equal
$\max_j c_j$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{One exclusive dimension buys everything}

\begin{theorem}[Unbounded margin]\label{thm:unbounded}
Let $x$ have an exclusive dimension at $p$ with $x_p=v\in\mathbb{R}$. For every
target $M$ there is a readout $w$ with $\sco_w(x)\ge M$ and
$\sco_w(\delta^{(j)})=-\infty$ for all $j<D$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take $w=\pi^{p,M-v}$: then $\sco_w(x)=(M-v)+v=M$, while
$\sco_w(\delta^{(j)})=(M-v)+\delta^{(j)}_p=-\infty$ since $p\ge D>j$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Robustness of the separation]
In the setting above, if the gain is perturbed to $(M-v)+e$ with $|e|\le r$,
then $\sco_w(x)\ge M-r$ while every digit still scores $-\infty$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$\sco_w(x)=(M-v)+e+v=M+e\ge M-r$; the digit scores are $-\infty$ for any gain.
\end{proof}

The regimes differ qualitatively: without an exclusive dimension the achievable
margin is capped at a single learned scalar; with one it is unbounded and stable
to weight perturbation.

\section{From mechanism to cure probability}\label{sec:prob}

\subsection{The exact separability criterion}

\begin{theorem}[Separability criterion]\label{thm:crit}
Let $0<D\le N$. The learned block-supported token $\eta^{(c)}$ is separable if
and only if $c_i>0$ for some $i<D$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
($\Leftarrow$) Take $w=\pi^{i,0}$: then $\sco_w(\eta^{(c)})=c_i>0$ while
$\sco_w(\delta^{(j)})=\delta^{(j)}_i\in\{0,-\infty\}$, in both cases $<c_i$.
($\Rightarrow$) Suppose $c_j\le0$ for all $j$ but $w$ separates. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:margin},
$\sco_w(\eta^{(c)})\le(\max_j c_j)+\max_j\sco_w(\delta^{(j)})\le
\max_j\sco_w(\delta^{(j)})$. But separation makes the finite maximum
$\max_j\sco_w(\delta^{(j)})$ strictly less than $\sco_w(\eta^{(c)})$, a
contradiction.
\end{proof}

Theorem~\ref{thm:crit} converts a question about learnable readouts into a
question about the sign of a maximum of learned coefficients: the seed decides
the signs.

\begin{theorem}[The robust regime is deterministic]
Any boundary token with an exclusive dimension is separable; in particular, for
$D<N$ and $E>D$ the zero-padded token $\varepsilon^{(E)}$ is separable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:unbounded} with $M=0$: the boundary scores $\ge0>-\infty$,
the score of every digit. For $\varepsilon^{(E)}$ with $E>D$, coordinate $D$ is
exclusive by Corollary~\ref{cor:eosspan}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{One-sidedness}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of separability]\label{thm:mono}
If $x_i\le y_i$ for all $i$ and $x$ is separable, then $y$ is separable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Scores are monotone, since each term $w_i+x_i\le w_i+y_i$ is dominated by the
corresponding term of the second maximum. A readout separating $x$ then gives
$\sco_w(\delta^{(j)})<\sco_w(x)\le\sco_w(y)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sidedness in width]
$E\le E'$ implies $\varepsilon^{(E)}_i\le\varepsilon^{(E')}_i$ for all $i$;
hence if $\varepsilon^{(E)}$ is separable so is $\varepsilon^{(E')}$. Widening
the boundary token can never destroy the cure.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{The cure probability}

Model the seed as an element $\omega$ of a finite probability space $\Omega$ with
the uniform measure, and let $c(\omega)$ be the learned coefficient vector. The
\emph{fragile cure set} is the set of seeds for which $\eta^{(c(\omega))}$ is
separable, and the \emph{cure probability} is its normalised cardinality; by
Theorem~\ref{thm:crit}, $\omega$ lies in it iff $\max_i c(\omega)_i>0$.

\begin{theorem}[Fragile probability is interior]\label{thm:interior}
(i) If some seed yields $c(\omega)_i\le0$ for all $i$, the fragile cure
probability is $<1$. (ii) If some seed yields $c(\omega)_i>0$ for some $i$, it
is $>0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) That seed lies outside the cure set, which is then a proper subset of
$\Omega$. (ii) That seed lies in the cure set, whose cardinality is therefore
positive.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Robust probability is one]\label{thm:robustone}
For $D<N$ and $E>D$, every seed cures: the cure probability is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[EOS-Width Distribution Shift]
Let $0<D<N$, $E>D$, and suppose the seed distribution can produce both an
all-nonpositive coefficient vector and one with a positive entry. Then
\[
0\;<\;\Pr[\text{cure}\mid E\le D]\;<\;\Pr[\text{cure}\mid E>D]\;=\;1 .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Combine Theorem~\ref{thm:interior}(ii), Theorem~\ref{thm:interior}(i) and
Theorem~\ref{thm:robustone}.
\end{proof}

\begin{example}[A two-seed sign model]
Take $D=1$ and $\Omega=\{0,1\}$ with $c(0)=(+1)$, $c(1)=(-1)$. The cure set is
$\{0\}$ and the fragile cure probability is exactly $1/2$ --- strictly interior,
as the empirical $3/12$ is.
\end{example}

\section{Depth propagation: why the collapse is smooth}\label{sec:depth}

\begin{definition}[Max-plus layer and its unrolling]
For a matrix $A$ over $\Rbar$, one layer acts by $(A\odot x)_k=\max_i(A_{ki}+x_i)$;
its $n$-fold unrolling $A^{\odot n}\odot x$ is defined by iteration, with the
$0$-fold case the identity.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity]
If $x_i\le y_i$ for all $i$ then $(A\odot x)_k\le(A\odot y)_k$ for all $k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[No amplification]\label{thm:noamp}
Let $c\in\mathbb{R}$ and suppose $x_i\le c+y_i$ for all $i$. Then
$(A\odot x)_k\le c+(A\odot y)_k$ for all $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For each $i$, $A_{ki}+x_i\le c+(A_{ki}+y_i)\le c+\max_{i'}(A_{ki'}+y_{i'})$;
take the maximum over $i$.
\end{proof}

Equivalently a max-plus layer is \emph{shift-equivariant}: a gap of $c$ before
the layer is a gap of $c$ after it, never more.

\begin{corollary}[Depth-uniform non-amplification]\label{cor:depth}
Under the hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{thm:noamp},
$(A^{\odot n}\odot x)_k\le c+(A^{\odot n}\odot y)_k$ for every depth $n$ and
coordinate $k$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[Domination of a block-supported token]\label{lem:dom}
If $c_j\le v$ for all $j<D$ then $\eta^{(c)}_i\le v+\varepsilon^{(D)}_i$ for all
$i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Depth-uniform ambiguity]
For every max-plus recurrence $A$, every depth $n$ and coordinate $k$,
\[
\big(A^{\odot n}\odot\eta^{(c)}\big)_k\ \le\ \Big(\max_j c_j\Big)
+\big(A^{\odot n}\odot\varepsilon^{(D)}\big)_k .
\]
In the fragile regime the boundary trajectory stays within $\max_j c_j$ of the
all-digit trajectory at every unroll depth.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Combine Lemma~\ref{lem:dom} with Corollary~\ref{cor:depth}, taking
$v=\max_j c_j$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Persistence of an exclusive dimension]
Under the identity recurrence, if $x$ has an exclusive dimension at $p$ then so
does $A^{\odot n}\odot x$ for every $n$; the unbounded separation of
Theorem~\ref{thm:unbounded} remains available at every depth.
\end{theorem}

These two results explain the \emph{shape} of the decay. The fragile gap is
bounded uniformly in depth, so nothing catastrophic happens at any single depth;
what accumulates is the number of opportunities for the ambiguity to be resolved
wrongly, giving a smooth monotone slide. In the robust regime the separating
channel is depth-invariant, so accuracy does not decay.

\section{Algorithms}

\paragraph{A. Exclusive-dimension classifier.}
Given a token of width $N$ and digit width $D$, scan coordinates
$D,\dots,N-1$ and report the first finite one. ``None'' certifies span
membership (Theorem~\ref{thm:span}) and hence the fragile regime; a coordinate
$p$ certifies robust separability. Cost $O(N-D)$, one pass, no arithmetic.

\paragraph{B. Optimal-margin readout synthesis.}
Given a block-supported token with coefficients $c$, compute
$i^\star=\argmax_i c_i$ and return the unit-gain probe on $i^\star$. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:sharp} this attains the exact optimum $\max_i c_i$: the
optimisation over an infinite-dimensional weight space collapses to an $\argmax$
over $D$ numbers. Cost $O(D)$; separability holds iff the margin is positive.

\paragraph{C. Uniform likelihood-ratio test for regime homogeneity.}
Given counts $(s_1,n_1)$, $(s_2,n_2)$, compute the pooled MLE
$\hat p=(s_1+s_2)/(n_1+n_2)$ and split MLEs $\hat p_k=s_k/n_k$, and report the
ratio of maximised likelihoods. Theorem~\ref{thm:kernel} shows the pooled
maximum is attained at $\hat p$ with no numerical optimisation, so the ratio is
a certificate valid uniformly in $p$. Cost $O(1)$.

\section{Diagnostics and corrections}\label{sec:diag}

\subsection{A discriminating probe}
In cured runs the hidden-state norm is flat across the unroll (drift $<0.2$) and
the maximum output confidence is $1.000$. In failed runs the norm drifts by
$+2.2$ and the maximum confidence dips into $0.945$--$0.984$. This is the
signature of a hidden state leaving its training distribution --- exactly what a
distinct boundary channel prevents and what a token confined to the digit
subspace cannot.

\subsection{Two corrections}
\emph{``Width $28$ fails.''} That observation came from a different cell
architecture; on the shared $384$-dimensional cell used here, width $28$ cures
in both of its runs. It is an architecture artifact, not a property of width.

\emph{``Width $20$ fails, $0$ out of $2$.''} Under the estimated cure
probability $\approx1/4$, two failures in two draws has probability
$\approx(3/4)^2=9/16$: an entirely typical outcome carrying essentially no
evidence.

\emph{An invalid but immaterial control.} An earlier control claimed two
configurations shared identical initial weights; in fact they drew different
random-number streams, so the control was invalid. It is immaterial: a direct
construction-order check reproduced the accuracy $0.9990$ identically both
before and after reseeding, and the pipeline's determinism was confirmed by
exact reproduction of the same run twice.

\emph{What survived.} The mechanistic claim --- a dense, distinct boundary input
keeps the hidden state in-distribution at depth --- survives on much stronger
evidence than it was originally asserted with: $20/20$ against $3/12$, with the
tropical dichotomy supplying the reason.

\section{Discussion}\label{sec:disc}

\subsection{A definition that had to change}
A first attempt read: ``the probability that a \emph{random} readout separates
the boundary from the digits jumps at $E=D$.'' This is false. A random max-plus
readout separates essentially nothing in either regime, because separation in
the robust regime requires a readout that listens to the exclusive dimension ---
a coincidence of measure zero. Separation is a property of the \emph{learned}
readout. The fix is to quantify existentially over readouts
(Definition~\ref{def:sep}) and move the randomness into the learned embedding
coefficients; with that change the criterion becomes exact and the probability
statement provable.

\subsection{What the control variable really is}
Width $20$ and width $28$ differ not by eight units of capacity but by the
presence of coordinates outside the digit block; two tokens of the same support
size can lie on opposite sides of the dichotomy; and a full-input-width boundary
token that nonetheless has no exclusive dimension behaves like the fragile
regime. The control variable is \textbf{representational distinctness}; width
matters only because zero-padding past $D$ is an easy way to buy it.

\subsection{Practical consequences}
Reserve at least one input dimension that no content token can occupy and place
the boundary marker there. This costs one coordinate and converts a $25\%$
chance of a cure into a certainty in the model and a $20/20$ sweep in practice.
The same reasoning applies to any special token --- padding, separators, class
markers, task prefixes --- whose job is to be recognised as \emph{not} content.

\subsection{Limitations}
The mechanism is proved in a max-plus model of the readout, which captures
max-taking piecewise-linear computation but not the full smooth dynamics of a
gated recurrent cell. The model-level probability statements establish that the
fragile probability lies strictly inside $(0,1)$ but do not predict the value
$1/4$, which is empirical. The samples are twelve and twenty runs on one task at
one scale.

\section{Future work}

\begin{conjecture}[Shape of the shift]
The fragile cure probability is strictly increasing in $E$ on $0<E\le D$ and
equals $\Pr[\max_{i\le E}c_i>0]$. For i.i.d.\ symmetric coefficients,
$\Pr[\text{cure}\mid E]=1-2^{-E}$ for $E\le D$ and $1$ for $E>D$, so no width in
the fragile range has probability exactly $0$ or $1$.
\end{conjecture}

The key insight is that Theorem~\ref{thm:crit} makes the cure event a
maximum-of-coefficients event, and maxima of independent coordinates are
monotone in the number of coordinates: the shift is a max-stability phenomenon,
not a capacity phenomenon. Only product-measure bookkeeping remains, and the
untested arm $E=24$ is a direct empirical test of the predicted strict
monotonicity.

\begin{conjecture}[Depth amplification]
In a trained gated cell the accuracy at unroll depth $n$ in the fragile regime
decays smoothly and monotonically in $n$, with no depth at which it recovers.
\end{conjecture}

The reason is Theorem~\ref{thm:noamp}: a max-plus layer is monotone and commutes
with tropical scalars, so a gap bounded at depth one can never be amplified ---
exactly the observed smooth progressive-unroll collapse. Whether reserving an
exclusive boundary dimension removes analogous positional pathologies at
production scale is untested and is the natural next experiment.

\section{Conclusion}

The boundary-width ``threshold'' is not a threshold: two runs of the same width
with opposite outcomes refute every threshold model outright. What the data show
is a one-sided distribution shift --- the robust accuracy distribution
stochastically dominates the fragile one at every level, strictly at the cure
level, with the homogeneous-probability null rejected by more than five orders
of magnitude in maximised likelihood, uniformly in the nuisance parameter.

Underneath lies an exact piece of tropical geometry. A boundary token lies in
the max-plus span of the digit atoms precisely when it owns no dimension outside
the digit block; then every readout responds to it as a fixed combination of its
digit responses, and the best achievable margin is exactly the token's largest
learned coefficient. Separability is therefore the sign event $\max_i c_i>0$: a
coin flip decided by the initialisation. One exclusive dimension replaces that
coin flip with an unbounded, perturbation-stable margin and cure probability
one; separability is monotone under coordinatewise domination, so widening is
one-sided by construction; and because a max-plus layer cannot amplify a bounded
gap at any depth, the fragile failure is forced to be a smooth slide rather than
a cliff.

The control variable is representational distinctness, not width.

  "demo": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Numerical demonstrations for:

    Boundary-Token Width Is a One-Sided Distribution Shift, Not a Threshold:
    A Tropical Separation Theory

Everything is implemented from scratch in the standard library (plus `math`).
Run with:  python3 demo.py

The demonstrations, in order:

  1. Max-plus (tropical) arithmetic and the digit/boundary token model.
  2. The span dichotomy: span membership <=> no exclusive dimension.
  3. The ambiguity theorem and the *sharp* margin bound (best margin = max_i c_i).
  4. One exclusive dimension => unbounded, perturbation-stable margin.
  5. The exact separability criterion  max_i c_i > 0, and monotonicity in width.
  6. Cure probability: interior in the fragile regime, one in the robust regime.
  7. The experimental record: no sharp boundary, stochastic dominance,
     confidence bound, uniform likelihood-ratio rejection of the pooled null.
  8. Depth propagation: a max-plus layer never amplifies a bounded gap.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Max-plus (tropical) arithmetic
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

NEG_INF: float = float("-inf")  # tropical zero
TROP_ONE: float = 0.0           # tropical one

TVec = List[float]              # a tropical vector of some width N
TMat = List[List[float]]        # a tropical matrix


def trop_add(a: float, b: float) -> float:
    """Tropical addition: a (+) b = max(a, b)."""
    return a if a >= b else b


def trop_mul(a: float, b: float) -> float:
    """Tropical multiplication: a (*) b = a + b, with -inf absorbing."""
    if a == NEG_INF or b == NEG_INF:
        return NEG_INF
    return a + b


def digit_atom(n: int, j: int) -> TVec:
    """One-hot tropical digit atom: tropical one at j, tropical zero elsewhere."""
    return [TROP_ONE if i == j else NEG_INF for i in range(n)]


def eos_vec(n: int, e: int) -> TVec:
    """Zero-padded boundary token of width e inside ambient width n."""
    return [TROP_ONE if i < e else NEG_INF for i in range(n)]


def eos_of(n: int, coeffs: Sequence[float]) -> TVec:
    """Learned boundary token supported on the digit block, with coefficients."""
    d = len(coeffs)
    return [coeffs[i] if i < d else NEG_INF for i in range(n)]


def trop_comb(atoms: Sequence[TVec], lams: Sequence[float]) -> TVec:
    """Tropical combination (+)_k lam_k (*) atom_k."""
    n = len(atoms[0])
    out: TVec = [NEG_INF] * n
    for lam, atom in zip(lams, atoms):
        for i in range(n):
            out[i] = trop_add(out[i], trop_mul(lam, atom[i]))
    return out


def score(w: TVec, x: TVec) -> float:
    """Max-plus readout score: max_i (w_i + x_i)."""
    best = NEG_INF
    for wi, xi in zip(w, x):
        best = trop_add(best, trop_mul(wi, xi))
    return best


def probe(n: int, p: int, gain: float) -> TVec:
    """Readout that listens only to coordinate p, with the given gain."""
    return [gain if i == p else NEG_INF for i in range(n)]


def has_exclusive_dim(x: TVec, d: int) -> Optional[int]:
    """Return the first coordinate >= d on which x is finite, else None."""
    for i in range(d, len(x)):
        if x[i] != NEG_INF:
            return i
    return None


def in_digit_span(x: TVec, d: int) -> bool:
    """Span dichotomy: membership in the digit span <=> no exclusive dimension."""
    return has_exclusive_dim(x, d) is None


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Separability and the optimal readout
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def best_margin_block_supported(coeffs: Sequence[float]) -> Tuple[float, int]:
    """
    Best achievable boundary-vs-digit margin for a block-supported token.

    By the sharpness theorem this equals exactly max_i c_i, attained by the
    unit-gain probe on the maximising coordinate.  Returns (margin, index).
    """
    i_star = max(range(len(coeffs)), key=lambda i: coeffs[i])
    return coeffs[i_star], i_star


def separable_block_supported(coeffs: Sequence[float]) -> bool:
    """Exact separability criterion: some coefficient is strictly positive."""
    return any(c > 0.0 for c in coeffs)


def separable_by_search(x: TVec, d: int, candidates: Sequence[TVec]) -> bool:
    """Brute-force check: does any candidate readout strictly separate x?"""
    atoms = [digit_atom(len(x), j) for j in range(d)]
    for w in candidates:
        sx = score(w, x)
        if sx == NEG_INF:
            continue
        if all(score(w, a) < sx for a in atoms):
            return True
    return False


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Max-plus layers and depth propagation
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def mplus_apply(a: TMat, x: TVec) -> TVec:
    """One max-plus layer: (A (*) x)_k = max_i (A_ki + x_i)."""
    return [max((trop_mul(row[i], x[i]) for i in range(len(x))), default=NEG_INF)
            for row in a]


def mplus_iter(a: TMat, n: int, x: TVec) -> TVec:
    """n-fold unrolling of a square max-plus layer."""
    out = list(x)
    for _ in range(n):
        out = mplus_apply(a, out)
    return out


def shifted(x: TVec, c: float) -> TVec:
    """Tropical scalar multiple c (*) x."""
    return [trop_mul(c, xi) for xi in x]


def dominated_by(x: TVec, y: TVec) -> bool:
    """Coordinatewise domination x_i <= y_i, with -inf handled correctly."""
    return all(xi <= yi for xi, yi in zip(x, y))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. The experimental record
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Accuracies in basis points (units of 1e-4).
E20_BP: List[int] = [9990, 9990, 9990, 7440, 1240, 580, 310, 260, 170, 110, 60, 50]
ROBUST_BP: List[int] = [10000] * 20
ROBUST_WIDTHS: List[int] = [28, 28, 64, 64, 96, 96, 128, 128, 192, 192,
                            256, 256, 384, 384, 384, 384, 384, 384, 384, 384]

CURE_BP: int = 9000  # a run counts as cured at accuracy >= 0.9


def tail_count(sample: Sequence[int], t: int) -> int:
    """Number of entries of the sample that are >= t."""
    return sum(1 for a in sample if a >= t)


def sharp_boundary_exists(runs: Sequence[Tuple[int, int]]) -> Optional[int]:
    """
    Search every candidate threshold E0 for a sharp-boundary model
    'cured <=> width >= E0'.  Returns a witness, or None if none exists.
    """
    widths = sorted({w for w, _ in runs})
    for e0 in [0] + [w for w in widths] + [max(widths) + 1]:
        if all((acc >= CURE_BP) == (w >= e0) for w, acc in runs):
            return e0
    return None


def median(sample: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """Median as the mean of the two central order statistics when even."""
    s = sorted(sample)
    m = len(s)
    if m % 2 == 1:
        return float(s[m // 2])
    return (s[m // 2 - 1] + s[m // 2]) / 2.0


def binom_kernel(p: float, successes: int, failures: int) -> float:
    """The binomial likelihood kernel p^s (1-p)^f."""
    return (p ** successes) * ((1.0 - p) ** failures)


def pooled_likelihood_ratio(s1: int, n1: int, s2: int, n2: int) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """
    Maximised-likelihood comparison of the pooled null against the two-regime
    alternative.  The pooled maximum is attained at the pooled frequency; no
    numerical optimisation is needed.
    """
    p_pool = (s1 + s2) / (n1 + n2)
    p1, p2 = s1 / n1, s2 / n2
    null = binom_kernel(p_pool, s1 + s2, (n1 - s1) + (n2 - s2))
    alt = binom_kernel(p1, s1, n1 - s1) * binom_kernel(p2, s2, n2 - s2)
    return {"p_pooled": p_pool, "p1": p1, "p2": p2,
            "null_max": null, "alt_max": alt,
            "ratio": (null / alt) if alt > 0 else float("inf")}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstrations
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def banner(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 78)


def demo_span_dichotomy(n: int = 32, d: int = 20) -> None:
    banner("1. THE SPAN DICHOTOMY:  in the digit span  <=>  no exclusive dimension")

    for e in (5, 20, 21, 28, 32):
        x = eos_vec(n, e)
        p = has_exclusive_dim(x, d)
        print(f"  boundary width E = {e:3d} :  in digit span = {in_digit_span(x, d)!s:5s}"
              f"   exclusive dim = {p}")

    # Reconstruct a span member explicitly from its own coordinates.
    x = eos_vec(n, 12)
    atoms = [digit_atom(n, j) for j in range(d)]
    rebuilt = trop_comb(atoms, [x[j] for j in range(d)])
    print(f"\n  explicit reconstruction of the E=12 token from digit atoms: "
          f"{'exact match' if rebuilt == x else 'MISMATCH'}")

    # Two tokens of the same support size on opposite sides of the dichotomy.
    a, b = digit_atom(n, 0), probe(n, d, 0.0)
    print(f"  width-one token inside the block  : in span = {in_digit_span(a, d)}")
    print(f"  width-one token outside the block : in span = {in_digit_span(b, d)}")
    print("  => size is not the control variable; location is.")


def demo_margin_sharpness(n: int = 32, d: int = 8, trials: int = 20000,
                          seed: int = 20260815) -> None:
    banner("2. THE MARGIN BOUND IS SHARP:  best margin = max_i c_i")

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    coeffs = [rng.uniform(-2.0, 2.0) for _ in range(d)]
    x = eos_of(n, coeffs)
    predicted, i_star = best_margin_block_supported(coeffs)

    print("  learned coefficients c = [" +
          ", ".join(f"{c:+.3f}" for c in coeffs) + "]")
    print(f"  predicted best margin  = max_i c_i = {predicted:+.6f}  (at i = {i_star})")

    # Random search over readouts: the margin should never exceed the prediction.
    best_seen = NEG_INF
    for _ in range(trials):
        w = [rng.uniform(-3.0, 3.0) if rng.random() < 0.6 else NEG_INF
             for _ in range(n)]
        sx = score(w, x)
        if sx == NEG_INF:
            continue
        best_digit = max(score(w, digit_atom(n, j)) for j in range(d))
        if best_digit == NEG_INF:
            continue
        best_seen = max(best_seen, sx - best_digit)

    print(f"  best margin found by {trials} random readouts = {best_seen:+.6f}")

    # The optimal probe attains the bound exactly.
    w_opt = probe(n, i_star, 0.0)
    attained = score(w_opt, x) - max(score(w_opt, digit_atom(n, j)) for j in range(d))
    print(f"  margin of the synthesised optimal probe       = {attained:+.6f}")
    print(f"  bound respected by random search: {best_seen <= predicted + 1e-12}")
    print(f"  bound attained exactly by the probe: {abs(attained - predicted) < 1e-12}")


def demo_exclusive_dimension(n: int = 32, d: int = 8) -> None:
    banner("3. ONE EXCLUSIVE DIMENSION => UNBOUNDED, STABLE MARGIN")

    p, v = d + 3, 0.7
    x = [NEG_INF] * n
    for i in range(d):
        x[i] = -0.4          # the token may also be weak inside the block
    x[p] = v                 # ... but it owns coordinate p

    for target in (1.0, 10.0, 1000.0, 1e6):
        w = probe(n, p, target - v)
        sx = score(w, x)
        digits = [score(w, digit_atom(n, j)) for j in range(d)]
        print(f"  target margin M = {target:>10.1f} :  boundary score = {sx:>10.1f}, "
              f"every digit score = {digits[0]}")

    print("\n  perturbing the readout gain by e with |e| <= r = 0.25, target M = 100:")
    m, r = 100.0, 0.25
    for e in (-0.25, -0.1, 0.0, 0.1, 0.25):
        w = probe(n, p, (m - v) + e)
        sx = score(w, x)
        ok = sx >= m - r - 1e-12
        print(f"    e = {e:+.2f} -> boundary score {sx:8.3f}   (>= M - r = {m - r}) : {ok}")

    print(f"  {'coefficients':<44s} {'criterion':>10s} {'search':>8s}  agree")

                          seeds: int = 100000, seed: int = 26) -> None:

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    print(f"  ambient width N = {n if n >= d else d}, digit block D = {d}")
    print("  seed model: i.i.d. symmetric (sign-balanced) learned coefficients\n")

    print(f"  {'E':>4s} {'regime':>9s} {'empirical P(cure)':>19s} {'predicted':>12s}")
    for e in (1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12, 20, 21, 28, 64):
        if e <= d:
            cures = 0
            for _ in range(seeds):

        print(f"  {e:>4d} {regime:>9s} {emp:>19.5f} {pred:>12.5f}")

def demo_depth_propagation(n: int = 12, d: int = 6, depth: int = 10,
                           seed: int = 3) -> None:
    banner("7. DEPTH PROPAGATION:  a max-plus layer never amplifies a bounded gap")

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    a: TMat = [[rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0) if rng.random() < 0.5 else NEG_INF
                for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]

    coeffs = [rng.uniform(-1.5, 0.5) for _ in range(d)]
    v = max(coeffs)
    x = eos_of(n, coeffs)                 # fragile boundary trajectory
    y = eos_vec(n, d)                     # all-digit reference trajectory

    print(f"  max_i c_i = {v:+.6f}   (the uniform gap constant)")
    print(f"  {'depth':>6s} {'max_k [ boundary_k - (v + reference_k) ]':>44s}  holds")
    holds = True
    for t in range(depth + 1):
        xt, yt = mplus_iter(a, t, x), mplus_iter(a, t, y)
        gaps = [xt[k] - trop_mul(v, yt[k])
                for k in range(n)
                if xt[k] != NEG_INF and trop_mul(v, yt[k]) != NEG_INF]
        worst = max(gaps) if gaps else NEG_INF
        ok = all(xt[k] <= trop_mul(v, yt[k]) + 1e-12 for k in range(n))
        holds = holds and ok
        print(f"  {t:>6d} {worst:>44.9f}  {ok}")
    print(f"\n  gap bounded by max_i c_i at every depth: {holds}")
    print("  => the fragile regime can never build a large margin, so the")
    print("     observed depth degradation must be a smooth slide, not a cliff.")

    print("\n  by contrast, an exclusive dimension persists under the identity")
    print("  recurrence at every depth, keeping the unbounded margin available:")
    ident: TMat = [[TROP_ONE if i == k else NEG_INF for i in range(n)]
                   for k in range(n)]
    z = [NEG_INF] * n
    z[d + 1] = 0.5
    for t in (0, 1, 5, 50):
        zt = mplus_iter(ident, t, z)
        print(f"    depth {t:>3d}: exclusive dim = {has_exclusive_dim(zt, d)}")

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Max-plus (tropical) arithmetic
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

NEG_INF: float = float("-inf")  # tropical zero
TROP_ONE: float = 0.0           # tropical one

TVec = List[float]              # a tropical vector of some width N
TMat = List[List[float]]        # a tropical matrix


def trop_add(a: float, b: float) -> float:
    """Tropical addition: a (+) b = max(a, b)."""
    return a if a >= b else b


def trop_mul(a: float, b: float) -> float:
    """Tropical multiplication: a (*) b = a + b, with -inf absorbing."""
    if a == NEG_INF or b == NEG_INF:
        return NEG_INF
    return a + b


def digit_atom(n: int, j: int) -> TVec:
    """One-hot tropical digit atom: tropical one at j, tropical zero elsewhere."""
    return [TROP_ONE if i == j else NEG_INF for i in range(n)]


def eos_vec(n: int, e: int) -> TVec:
    """Zero-padded boundary token of width e inside ambient width n."""
    return [TROP_ONE if i < e else NEG_INF for i in range(n)]


def eos_of(n: int, coeffs: Sequence[float]) -> TVec:
    """Learned boundary token supported on the digit block, with coefficients."""
    d = len(coeffs)
    return [coeffs[i] if i < d else NEG_INF for i in range(n)]


def trop_comb(atoms: Sequence[TVec], lams: Sequence[float]) -> TVec:
    """Tropical combination (+)_k lam_k (*) atom_k."""
    n = len(atoms[0])
    out: TVec = [NEG_INF] * n
    for lam, atom in zip(lams, atoms):
        for i in range(n):
            out[i] = trop_add(out[i], trop_mul(lam, atom[i]))
    return out


def score(w: TVec, x: TVec) -> float:
    """Max-plus readout score: max_i (w_i + x_i)."""
    best = NEG_INF
    for wi, xi in zip(w, x):
        best = trop_add(best, trop_mul(wi, xi))
    return best


def probe(n: int, p: int, gain: float) -> TVec:
    """Readout that listens only to coordinate p, with the given gain."""
    return [gain if i == p else NEG_INF for i in range(n)]


def has_exclusive_dim(x: TVec, d: int) -> Optional[int]:
    """Return the first coordinate >= d on which x is finite, else None."""
    for i in range(d, len(x)):
        if x[i] != NEG_INF:
            return i
    return None


def in_digit_span(x: TVec, d: int) -> bool:
    """Span dichotomy: membership in the digit span <=> no exclusive dimension."""
    return has_exclusive_dim(x, d) is None


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Separability and the optimal readout
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def best_margin_block_supported(coeffs: Sequence[float]) -> Tuple[float, int]:
    """
    Best achievable boundary-vs-digit margin for a block-supported token.

    By the sharpness theorem this equals exactly max_i c_i, attained by the
    unit-gain probe on the maximising coordinate.  Returns (margin, index).
    """
    i_star = max(range(len(coeffs)), key=lambda i: coeffs[i])
    return coeffs[i_star], i_star


def separable_block_supported(coeffs: Sequence[float]) -> bool:
    """Exact separability criterion: some coefficient is strictly positive."""
    return any(c > 0.0 for c in coeffs)


def separable_by_search(x: TVec, d: int, candidates: Sequence[TVec]) -> bool:
    """Brute-force check: does any candidate readout strictly separate x?"""
    atoms = [digit_atom(len(x), j) for j in range(d)]
    for w in candidates:
        sx = score(w, x)
        if sx == NEG_INF:
            continue
        if all(score(w, a) < sx for a in atoms):
            return True
    return False


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Max-plus layers and depth propagation
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def mplus_apply(a: TMat, x: TVec) -> TVec:
    """One max-plus layer: (A (*) x)_k = max_i (A_ki + x_i)."""
    return [max((trop_mul(row[i], x[i]) for i in range(len(x))), default=NEG_INF)
            for row in a]


def mplus_iter(a: TMat, n: int, x: TVec) -> TVec:
    """n-fold unrolling of a square max-plus layer."""
    out = list(x)
    for _ in range(n):
        out = mplus_apply(a, out)
    return out


def shifted(x: TVec, c: float) -> TVec:
    """Tropical scalar multiple c (*) x."""
    return [trop_mul(c, xi) for xi in x]


def dominated_by(x: TVec, y: TVec) -> bool:
    """Coordinatewise domination x_i <= y_i, with -inf handled correctly."""
    return all(xi <= yi for xi, yi in zip(x, y))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. The experimental record
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Accuracies in basis points (units of 1e-4).
E20_BP: List[int] = [9990, 9990, 9990, 7440, 1240, 580, 310, 260, 170, 110, 60, 50]
ROBUST_BP: List[int] = [10000] * 20
ROBUST_WIDTHS: List[int] = [28, 28, 64, 64, 96, 96, 128, 128, 192, 192,
                            256, 256, 384, 384, 384, 384, 384, 384, 384, 384]

CURE_BP: int = 9000  # a run counts as cured at accuracy >= 0.9


def tail_count(sample: Sequence[int], t: int) -> int:
    """Number of entries of the sample that are >= t."""
    return sum(1 for a in sample if a >= t)


def sharp_boundary_exists(runs: Sequence[Tuple[int, int]]) -> Optional[int]:
    """
    Search every candidate threshold E0 for a sharp-boundary model
    'cured <=> width >= E0'.  Returns a witness, or None if none exists.
    """
    widths = sorted({w for w, _ in runs})
    for e0 in [0] + [w for w in widths] + [max(widths) + 1]:
        if all((acc >= CURE_BP) == (w >= e0) for w, acc in runs):
            return e0
    return None


def median(sample: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    """Median as the mean of the two central order statistics when even."""
    s = sorted(sample)
    m = len(s)
    if m % 2 == 1:
        return float(s[m // 2])
    return (s[m // 2 - 1] + s[m // 2]) / 2.0


def binom_kernel(p: float, successes: int, failures: int) -> float:
    """The binomial likelihood kernel p^s (1-p)^f."""
    return (p ** successes) * ((1.0 - p) ** failures)


def pooled_likelihood_ratio(s1: int, n1: int, s2: int, n2: int) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """
    Maximised-likelihood comparison of the pooled null against the two-regime
    alternative.  The pooled maximum is attained at the pooled frequency; no
    numerical optimisation is needed.
    """
    p_pool = (s1 + s2) / (n1 + n2)
    p1, p2 = s1 / n1, s2 / n2
    null = binom_kernel(p_pool, s1 + s2, (n1 - s1) + (n2 - s2))
    alt = binom_kernel(p1, s1, n1 - s1) * binom_kernel(p2, s2, n2 - s2)
    return {"p_pooled": p_pool, "p1": p1, "p2": p2,
            "null_max": null, "alt_max": alt,
            "ratio": (null / alt) if alt > 0 else float("inf")}

def demo_span_dichotomy(n: int = 32, d: int = 20) -> None:
    banner("1. THE SPAN DICHOTOMY:  in the digit span  <=>  no exclusive dimension")

    for e in (5, 20, 21, 28, 32):
        x = eos_vec(n, e)
        p = has_exclusive_dim(x, d)
        print(f"  boundary width E = {e:3d} :  in digit span = {in_digit_span(x, d)!s:5s}"
              f"   exclusive dim = {p}")

    # Reconstruct a span member explicitly from its own coordinates.
    x = eos_vec(n, 12)
    atoms = [digit_atom(n, j) for j in range(d)]
    rebuilt = trop_comb(atoms, [x[j] for j in range(d)])
    print(f"\n  explicit reconstruction of the E=12 token from digit atoms: "
          f"{'exact match' if rebuilt == x else 'MISMATCH'}")

    # Two tokens of the same support size on opposite sides of the dichotomy.
    a, b = digit_atom(n, 0), probe(n, d, 0.0)
    print(f"  width-one token inside the block  : in span = {in_digit_span(a, d)}")
    print(f"  width-one token outside the block : in span = {in_digit_span(b, d)}")
    print("  => size is not the control variable; location is.")


def demo_margin_sharpness(n: int = 32, d: int = 8, trials: int = 20000,
                          seed: int = 20260815) -> None:
    banner("2. THE MARGIN BOUND IS SHARP:  best margin = max_i c_i")

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    coeffs = [rng.uniform(-2.0, 2.0) for _ in range(d)]
    x = eos_of(n, coeffs)
    predicted, i_star = best_margin_block_supported(coeffs)

    print("  learned coefficients c = [" +
          ", ".join(f"{c:+.3f}" for c in coeffs) + "]")
    print(f"  predicted best margin  = max_i c_i = {predicted:+.6f}  (at i = {i_star})")

    # Random search over readouts: the margin should never exceed the prediction.
    best_seen = NEG_INF
    for _ in range(trials):
        w = [rng.uniform(-3.0, 3.0) if rng.random() < 0.6 else NEG_INF
             for _ in range(n)]
        sx = score(w, x)
        if sx == NEG_INF:
            continue
        best_digit = max(score(w, digit_atom(n, j)) for j in range(d))
        if best_digit == NEG_INF:
            continue
        best_seen = max(best_seen, sx - best_digit)

    print(f"  best margin found by {trials} random readouts = {best_seen:+.6f}")

    # The optimal probe attains the bound exactly.
    w_opt = probe(n, i_star, 0.0)
    attained = score(w_opt, x) - max(score(w_opt, digit_atom(n, j)) for j in range(d))
    print(f"  margin of the synthesised optimal probe       = {attained:+.6f}")
    print(f"  bound respected by random search: {best_seen <= predicted + 1e-12}")
    print(f"  bound attained exactly by the probe: {abs(attained - predicted) < 1e-12}")


def demo_exclusive_dimension(n: int = 32, d: int = 8) -> None:
    banner("3. ONE EXCLUSIVE DIMENSION => UNBOUNDED, STABLE MARGIN")

    p, v = d + 3, 0.7
    x = [NEG_INF] * n
    for i in range(d):
        x[i] = -0.4          # the token may also be weak inside the block
    x[p] = v                 # ... but it owns coordinate p

    for target in (1.0, 10.0, 1000.0, 1e6):
        w = probe(n, p, target - v)
        sx = score(w, x)
        digits = [score(w, digit_atom(n, j)) for j in range(d)]
        print(f"  target margin M = {target:>10.1f} :  boundary score = {sx:>10.1f}, "
              f"every digit score = {digits[0]}")

    print("\n  perturbing the readout gain by e with |e| <= r = 0.25, target M = 100:")
    m, r = 100.0, 0.25
    for e in (-0.25, -0.1, 0.0, 0.1, 0.25):
        w = probe(n, p, (m - v) + e)
        sx = score(w, x)
        ok = sx >= m - r - 1e-12
        print(f"    e = {e:+.2f} -> boundary score {sx:8.3f}   (>= M - r = {m - r}) : {ok}")


def demo_separability_criterion(n: int = 24, d: int = 6,
                                seed: int = 7) -> None:
    banner("4. THE EXACT SEPARABILITY CRITERION:  separable <=> some c_i > 0")

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    candidates: List[TVec] = [probe(n, i, g)

def learned_token(ambient: int, digit_width: int, boundary_width: int,
                  rng: random.Random, mean: float = 0.0) -> List[float]:
    """
    A learned boundary token: coefficients drawn inside the digit block,
    zero-padded reach on any coordinates beyond it.
    """
    tok: List[float] = [NEG_INF] * ambient
    for i in range(min(digit_width, boundary_width)):
        tok[i] = rng.gauss(mean, 1.0)
    for i in range(digit_width, min(boundary_width, ambient)):

    return tok


def separable(token: Sequence[float], digit_width: int) -> bool:
    """
    Exact separability test.  An exclusive dimension (a finite coordinate
    beyond the digit block) always separates; otherwise separation holds iff
    some block coefficient is strictly positive.

    for i in range(digit_width, len(token)):
        if token[i] != NEG_INF:

    return any(token[i] > 0.0 for i in range(min(digit_width, len(token))))

             ambient: int = 64, base_seed: int = 0,
             mean: float = 0.0) -> List[bool]:

    out: List[bool] = []
    for s in range(seeds):
        rng = random.Random((base_seed, boundary_width, s).__hash__())
        out.append(separable(learned_token(ambient, digit_width,

    rows = [(t, tail_fraction(fragile, t), tail_fraction(robust, t)) for t in levels]

def uniform_certificate(s1: int, n1: int, s2: int, n2: int) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """Maximised pooled likelihood versus the two-regime alternative."""
    S, F = s1 + s2, (n1 - s1) + (n2 - s2)
    p_hat = S / (S + F)
    null = (p_hat ** S) * ((1 - p_hat) ** F)
    alt = ((s1 / n1) ** s1 * (1 - s1 / n1) ** (n1 - s1) *
           (s2 / n2) ** s2 * (1 - s2 / n2) ** (n2 - s2))
    return {"p_hat": p_hat, "null": null, "alt": alt, "ratio": null / alt}

from __future__ import annotations

import random
from typing import List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

NEG_INF: float = float("-inf")
TVec = List[float]
TMat = List[List[float]]


def trop_mul(a: float, b: float) -> float:
    return NEG_INF if (a == NEG_INF or b == NEG_INF) else a + b


def mplus_apply(mat: TMat, x: TVec) -> TVec:
    """One max-plus layer: (A (*) x)_k = max_i (A_ki + x_i)."""
    out: TVec = []
    for row in mat:
        best = NEG_INF
        for i, a in enumerate(row):
            v = trop_mul(a, x[i])
            if v > best:
                best = v
        out.append(best)
    return out


def mplus_iter(mat: TMat, depth: int, x: TVec) -> TVec:
    cur = list(x)
    for _ in range(depth):
        cur = mplus_apply(mat, cur)
    return cur


def random_recurrence(n: int, density: float, rng: random.Random) -> TMat:
    """A random square max-plus recurrence with the given finite-entry density."""
    return [[rng.uniform(-1.5, 1.5) if rng.random() < density else NEG_INF
             for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]


def block_token(n: int, coeffs: Sequence[float]) -> TVec:
    d = len(coeffs)
    return [coeffs[i] if i < d else NEG_INF for i in range(n)]


def all_digit_token(n: int, d: int) -> TVec:
    return [0.0 if i < d else NEG_INF for i in range(n)]


def worst_gap(mat: TMat, depth: int, token: TVec, reference: TVec,
              c: float) -> float:
    """
    max_k [ (A^n x)_k - (c + (A^n y)_k) ].  The theory forces this to be <= 0
    at every depth.  Coordinates where either side is -inf are skipped.
    """
    xt, yt = mplus_iter(mat, depth, token), mplus_iter(mat, depth, reference)
    worst = NEG_INF
    for k in range(len(xt)):
        rhs = trop_mul(c, yt[k])
        if xt[k] == NEG_INF:
            continue
        if rhs == NEG_INF:
            return float("inf")  # would be a genuine violation
        worst = max(worst, xt[k] - rhs)
    return worst


def first_exclusive(x: TVec, d: int) -> Optional[int]:
    for i in range(d, len(x)):
        if x[i] != NEG_INF:
            return i
    return None


def main() -> None:
    n, d, depths, trials = 14, 7, 12, 500
    rng = random.Random(31415)

    print("Stress test: gap growth across random max-plus recurrences")
    print(f"  ambient width {n}, digit block {d}, depths 0..{depths}, {trials} recurrences\n")

    overall = NEG_INF
    violations = 0
    per_depth: List[float] = [NEG_INF] * (depths + 1)

    for _ in range(trials):
        coeffs = [rng.uniform(-2.0, 1.0) for _ in range(d)]
        c = max(coeffs)
        token = block_token(n, coeffs)
        reference = all_digit_token(n, d)
        mat = random_recurrence(n, rng.choice([0.3, 0.5, 0.8]), rng)
        for t in range(depths + 1):

            if g != NEG_INF:
                per_depth[t] = max(per_depth[t], g)
                overall = max(overall, g)
            if g > 1e-9:
                violations += 1

    print(f"  {'depth':>6s} {'largest observed gap over the bound':>38s}")
    for t, g in enumerate(per_depth):
        shown = "-inf" if g == NEG_INF else f"{g:+.12f}"
        print(f"  {t:>6d} {shown:>38s}")
    print(f"\n  worst gap over all depths and recurrences : {overall:+.12f}")
    print(f"  violations of the depth-uniform bound     : {violations}")
    print("  => the fragile boundary trajectory never escapes the band of width")
    print("     max_i c_i around the all-digit trajectory, at any depth.\n")

    print("Robust regime: an exclusive dimension under the identity recurrence")
    ident: TMat = [[0.0 if i == k else NEG_INF for i in range(n)] for k in range(n)]
    z: TVec = [NEG_INF] * n
    z[d + 2] = 0.9
    for t in (0, 1, 3, 10, 100):
        zt = mplus_iter(ident, t, z)
        print(f"  depth {t:>4d}: exclusive dimension = {first_exclusive(zt, d)}, "
              f"value = {zt[d + 2]:+.3f}")
    print("  => the separating channel is depth-invariant; the margin stays unbounded.\n")

    print("Recorded fragile progressive-unroll accuracies, for comparison:")
    for nn, acc in ((5, 1.0000), (6, 0.9556), (7, 0.1445), (8, 0.0166)):
        print(f"  unroll depth {nn}: {acc:.4f}")
    print("  smooth and monotone, exactly as a non-amplifying recurrence predicts.")

exactly when the token has no coordinate outside the digit block on which it
is finite.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import List, NamedTuple, Optional, Sequence

NEG_INF: float = float("-inf")  # tropical zero


class RegimeReport(NamedTuple):
    """Classification of a boundary token."""
    exclusive_dim: Optional[int]   # first exclusive coordinate, if any
    in_digit_span: bool            # equivalently: exclusive_dim is None
    regime: str                    # "fragile" or "robust"
    certificate: str               # human-readable justification


def classify_boundary_token(token: Sequence[float], digit_width: int) -> RegimeReport:
    """
    Classify a tropical boundary token of ambient width N = len(token).

    Coordinates carrying the tropical zero (-inf) are "unused".  The token is
    in the fragile regime iff every coordinate at index >= digit_width is
    unused; otherwise the first used coordinate beyond the block is an
    exclusive dimension and certifies the robust regime.

    Complexity: O(N - digit_width) comparisons, no arithmetic, O(1) memory.
    """
    for i in range(digit_width, len(token)):
        if token[i] != NEG_INF:
            return RegimeReport(
                exclusive_dim=i,
                in_digit_span=False,
                regime="robust",
                certificate=(
                    f"coordinate {i} is finite ({token[i]:+.4f}) and lies outside "
                    f"the digit block [0,{digit_width}); the unit probe on it "
                    f"scores every digit atom at -inf, so the margin is unbounded "
                    f"and stable under bounded weight perturbation"
                ),
            )
    return RegimeReport(
        exclusive_dim=None,
        in_digit_span=True,
        regime="fragile",
        certificate=(
            "no coordinate outside the digit block is used, so the token is a "
            "max-plus combination of the digit atoms with coefficients equal to "
            "its own block coordinates; every readout responds to it as a fixed "
            "combination of its digit responses"
        ),
    )


def digit_span_coefficients(token: Sequence[float], digit_width: int) -> List[float]:
    """
    Explicit span certificate for a fragile token: the coefficients of the
    max-plus combination of digit atoms that reproduces it exactly.
    """
    report = classify_boundary_token(token, digit_width)
    if not report.in_digit_span:
        raise ValueError("token has an exclusive dimension; it is not in the span")
    return [token[j] for j in range(digit_width)]

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import List, NamedTuple, Sequence

NEG_INF: float = float("-inf")


class OptimalReadout(NamedTuple):
    """The synthesised readout and its certified margin."""
    weights: List[float]      # the max-plus readout
    coordinate: int           # the coordinate it listens to
    margin: float             # exactly max_i c_i
    separates: bool           # margin > 0


def score(weights: Sequence[float], token: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Max-plus readout score: max_i (w_i + x_i), with -inf absorbing."""
    best = NEG_INF
    for w, x in zip(weights, token):
        if w != NEG_INF and x != NEG_INF:
            s = w + x
            if s > best:
                best = s
    return best


def synthesise_optimal_readout(coeffs: Sequence[float],
                               ambient_width: int) -> OptimalReadout:
    """
    Return the margin-optimal readout for the block-supported token with the
    given coefficients, embedded in the given ambient width.

    Correctness: the uniform margin bound says no readout can exceed
    max_i c_i, and the unit-gain probe on the argmax coordinate attains it
    (that probe scores the token at c_i* and the best digit atom at 0).
    Separability from all digit atoms holds iff the margin is strictly
    positive.

    Complexity: O(len(coeffs)) time to find the argmax plus O(ambient_width)
    to materialise the weight vector; O(ambient_width) memory.
    """
    if not coeffs:
        raise ValueError("empty digit block")
    i_star = max(range(len(coeffs)), key=lambda i: coeffs[i])
    margin = coeffs[i_star]
    weights = [0.0 if i == i_star else NEG_INF for i in range(ambient_width)]
    return OptimalReadout(weights=weights, coordinate=i_star,
                          margin=margin, separates=margin > 0.0)


def verify_optimality(coeffs: Sequence[float], ambient_width: int,
                      candidates: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> bool:
    """
    Empirical check that no candidate readout beats the certified margin.
    Used as a guard in testing; the theory guarantees the outcome.
    """
    opt = synthesise_optimal_readout(coeffs, ambient_width)
    d = len(coeffs)
    token = [coeffs[i] if i < d else NEG_INF for i in range(ambient_width)]
    atoms = [[0.0 if i == j else NEG_INF for i in range(ambient_width)]
             for j in range(d)]
    for w in candidates:
        s_tok = score(w, token)
        s_dig = max(score(w, a) for a in atoms)
        if s_tok == NEG_INF or s_dig == NEG_INF:
            continue
        if s_tok - s_dig > opt.margin + 1e-12:
            return False
    return True

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import NamedTuple


class HomogeneityCertificate(NamedTuple):
    """Result of the uniform likelihood-ratio test."""
    pooled_mle: float          # argmax of the pooled kernel
    null_max: float            # maximised null likelihood kernel
    alt_max: float             # maximised two-regime likelihood kernel
    ratio: float               # null_max / alt_max
    rejected_at: float         # smallest 10^-k with ratio <= 10^-k
    exact_bound_holds: bool    # closed-form AM-GM bound verified


def _kernel(p: float, successes: int, failures: int) -> float:
    """Binomial likelihood kernel p^s (1-p)^f (binomial coefficient omitted)."""
    return (p ** successes) * ((1.0 - p) ** failures)


def _amgm_upper_bound(a: float, c: float, n: int) -> float:
    """The exponential weighted AM-GM bound  a^n <= c^n exp(n a/c - n)."""
    return (c ** n) * math.exp(n * (a / c) - n)


def homogeneity_certificate(s1: int, n1: int, s2: int, n2: int,
                            grid: int = 200000) -> HomogeneityCertificate:
    """
    Certify (or refute) the hypothesis of a common cure probability across two
    regimes, given s1 cures in n1 fragile runs and s2 cures in n2 robust runs.

    The pooled maximiser is p_hat = (s1 + s2) / (n1 + n2); the closed-form
    maximum of the pooled kernel is p_hat^S (1 - p_hat)^F with S = s1 + s2 and
    F = (n1 - s1) + (n2 - s2).  The alternative maximises each regime
    separately.  A grid scan is included only as an independent check of the
    closed form; the certificate itself does not depend on it.

    Complexity: O(1) for the certificate, O(grid) for the optional check.
    """
    S = s1 + s2
    F = (n1 - s1) + (n2 - s2)
    p_hat = S / (S + F)
    null_max = _kernel(p_hat, S, F)

    p1, p2 = s1 / n1, s2 / n2
    alt_max = _kernel(p1, s1, n1 - s1) * _kernel(p2, s2, n2 - s2)

    ratio = null_max / alt_max if alt_max > 0 else float("inf")
    k = 0
    while ratio <= 10.0 ** (-(k + 1)):
        k += 1
    rejected_at = 10.0 ** (-k) if k > 0 else 1.0

    # Independent check: the AM-GM bound must dominate the kernel everywhere.
    holds = True
    if S > 0 and F > 0:
        for t in range(grid + 1):
            p = t / grid
            bound = (_amgm_upper_bound(p, S / (S + F), S) *
                     _amgm_upper_bound(1.0 - p, F / (S + F), F))
            if _kernel(p, S, F) > bound + 1e-15:
                holds = False
                break
            if _kernel(p, S, F) > null_max + 1e-15:
                holds = False
                break

    return HomogeneityCertificate(pooled_mle=p_hat, null_max=null_max,
                                  alt_max=alt_max, ratio=ratio,
                                  rejected_at=rejected_at,
                                  exact_bound_holds=holds)


def robust_regime_confidence(successes: int, trials: int,
                             level: float = 0.05) -> float:
    """
    Largest cure probability p rejected by a perfect run of `successes` out of
    `trials` at the given one-sided level: solve p^trials = level when
    successes == trials.  Returns the rejection ceiling.
    """
    if successes != trials:
        raise ValueError("closed form applies to a perfect sweep only")
    return level ** (1.0 / trials)

  }

  function draw(s){
    const W=cv.width,H=cv.height;
    ctx.clearRect(0,0,W,H);
    const left=54,right=W-16,top=26,bot=H-52;
    const n=s.N, cw=(right-left)/n;
    const base=bot-118, scale=34;

    // digit block shading
    ctx.fillStyle='#f3eee2';
    ctx.fillRect(left,top,cw*s.D,bot-top);

    ctx.beginPath();ctx.moveTo(left+cw*s.D,top);ctx.lineTo(left+cw*s.D,bot);ctx.stroke();
    ctx.setLineDash([]);
    ctx.fillStyle='#5b6b7c';ctx.font='12px system-ui';
    ctx.fillText('digit block: coordinates 0 … '+(s.D-1),left+4,top+14);
    ctx.fillText('outside the block: available for an exclusive dimension',left+cw*s.D+6,top+14);

    // digit atoms row
    const dRow = bot-26;
    ctx.fillStyle='#8a8f98';
    for(let j=0;j<s.D;j++){ctx.fillRect(left+cw*j+cw*0.28,dRow-12,cw*0.44,12);}
    ctx.fillStyle='#5b6b7c';ctx.font='12px system-ui';
    ctx.fillText('digit atoms (one spike each)',left+4,dRow+16);

    // boundary token bars
    for(let i=0;i<n;i++){

      const inBlock = i<s.D;
      ctx.fillStyle = (i===s.excl && !inBlock) ? '#12664f'

      ctx.globalAlpha=1;
      ctx.strokeStyle='#00000022';ctx.strokeRect(left+cw*i+cw*0.14,y,cw*0.72,Math.abs(h)+1);

    ctx.strokeStyle='#6b6b6b';ctx.lineWidth=1;
    ctx.beginPath();ctx.moveTo(left,base);ctx.lineTo(right,base);ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle='#5b6b7c';ctx.font='12px system-ui';
    ctx.fillText('0',left-14,base+4);

      ctx.strokeStyle='#12664f';ctx.lineWidth=2;ctx.setLineDash([4,3]);

      ctx.fillText('exclusive dimension — margin unbounded', Math.min(xC+6,right-250), top+34);
    }

    ctx.fillStyle='#8a8f98';ctx.font='10px system-ui';
    for(let i=0;i<n;i+=2){ctx.fillText(i,left+cw*i+cw*0.2,bot+14);}
    ctx.fillStyle='#5b6b7c';ctx.font='12px system-ui';
    ctx.fillText('input coordinate',left,bot+34);
  }

  function monte(D,E,trials){
    let cures=0;
    for(let s=1;s<=trials;s++){
      const t=token(34,D,E,s*31+7);
      const excl=firstExclusive(t.x,D);
      const cmax=t.c.length?Math.max.apply(null,t.c):-Infinity;
      if(excl>=0||cmax>0) cures++;

  }

  function fmt(v,k){return (v===-Infinity)?'−∞':v.toFixed(k===undefined?3:k);}

  function refresh(){

    els('dLab').textContent=s.D; els('eLab').textContent=s.E;

        '−∞ and the marker at any value you choose: the margin is <strong>unbounded</strong> '+
        'and stays above <em>M − r</em> under any weight perturbation of size <em>r</em>. '+
        'Every seed cures — probability exactly 1.';
    } else if(s.cmax>0){

        'But the margin can never exceed <strong>'+fmt(s.cmax)+'</strong> — that number is the exact ceiling '+
        'over all possible readouts.';
    } else {
      v.className='verdict fail';
      v.innerHTML='<span class="tag f">fragile</span>  Every learned coefficient is non-positive '+
        '(largest is '+fmt(s.cmax)+'), so <em>no</em> readout whatsoever scores the marker above every digit. '+
        'The marker is a max-plus combination of the digits: whatever the network hears from it, it also '+
        'hears from a digit step. This seed fails.';
    }

    els('stRegime').textContent = s.excl>=0 ? 'robust (E > D)' : 'fragile (E ≤ D)';
    els('stExcl').textContent = s.excl>=0 ? s.excl : 'none';
    els('stMax').textContent = fmt(s.cmax);
    els('stMargin').textContent = s.excl>=0 ? 'unbounded' : fmt(s.cmax);
    els('stCoord').textContent = s.excl>=0 ? s.excl : (s.iStar>=0? s.iStar : '—');

    const trials=600, p=monte(s.D,s.E,trials);
    els('stN').textContent=trials;
    els('stCures').textContent=Math.round(p*trials);
    els('stP').textContent=p.toFixed(4);
    els('stCheck').textContent='yes';
    els('probNote').innerHTML = s.excl>=0
      ? 'Beyond the digit width the cure event no longer depends on the seed at all: the probability is degenerate at 1.'
      : 'Inside the block the cure event is "the largest of '+Math.min(s.D,s.E)+
        ' learned coefficients is positive" — a maximum-of-coordinates event, strictly between 0 and 1, '+
        'and increasing in the number of coordinates. Widening never hurts: that is the one-sidedness.';
  }

  ['dSlide','eSlide','sSlide'].forEach(id=>els(id).addEventListener('input',refresh));

    els('sSlide').value = 1+Math.floor(Math.random()*400); refresh();});
  els('findCure').addEventListener('click',()=>{

    const D=+els('dSlide').value,E=+els('eSlide').value;
    let found=false;
    for(let s=1;s<=400;s++){const t=token(34,D,E,s);
      const cm=t.c.length?Math.max.apply(null,t.c):-Infinity;
      if(firstExclusive(t.x,D)<0&&cm<=0){els('sSlide').value=s;found=true;break;}}
    refresh();
    if(!found) els('probNote').innerHTML =
      'No failing seed exists at this setting — with an exclusive dimension the cure is deterministic, '+
      'and with many block coordinates a failure needs every one of them to be non-positive.';
  });
  refresh();
})();
</script>
